task_description: Add a realtime multiplayer quiz battle (リアルタイム対戦, feature ②) to the cost-minimal serverless quiz app. A Cognito-authenticated HOST creates a room from an existing registered quiz and shares a room ID; unauthenticated PARTICIPANTS join with a display name + room ID; the host starts and advances question by question; everyone sees the same synced question and a live scoreboard of participant names + individual scores. Transport is a NEW API Gateway v2 WebSocket API + a dedicated ARM64 ws Lambda + the existing DynamoDB single table (with TTL for cleanup), keeping the cost-minimal posture (on-demand DynamoDB, no VPC/NAT). Scoring is server-side reusing the stored answerIndex, which is never sent to participant clients. Additive only: the existing HTTP API, single-player flows, admin flows, history, and seeds are preserved. Frontend uses only the native browser WebSocket (deps stay exactly react + react-dom). Commit onto branch feat/realtime-battle; do not push or open a PR.

verification.semantic_review: APPROVED (v2 after 1 fix iteration; v1 NEEDS_CHANGES with 6 findings all resolved in commit 3999c14: host-away/reattach instead of fatal disconnect, atomic conditional join, guarded start/next transitions, token_use==='id', participant PLAYER# pruning, extracted+unit-tested validateTokenClaims)
verification.summary: Sandbox is INTEGRATIONS_ONLY: npm registry returns 403, so `npm ci`/`npm run build`/`npm test`/`npx cdk synth` and the frontend `npm install`/`vite build` CANNOT run here (confirmed: `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm ci` fails). There is no Dockerfile and no frontend test runner. Verification was therefore read-based and correct-by-construction. Confirmed: (1) working tree clean, 4 commits on feat/realtime-battle (FEAT-001..004); (2) lib/quiz-app-stack.ts adds a WEBSOCKET API + prod stage + ws ARM64 Lambda + grantManageConnections + DynamoDB TTL('ttl') + WebSocketEndpoint output + index.html Cognito callback/logout URLs, leaving the HTTP API/7 routes/JWT authorizer/Cognito/quiz item shapes intact; (3) lambda/ws.ts keeps all AWS SDK usage out of its exported pure helpers, verifies host Cognito JWTs (RS256 via node:crypto + JWKS) for create/control actions while participants join with name+roomId only, scores server-side using the stored answerIndex, and NEVER places answerIndex in any broadcast (only toParticipantQuestion is sent); (4) test/quiz-app-stack.test.ts keeps all prior assertions (scoped by RouteKey) and adds WebSocket API/routes/stage, 2 ARM64 Lambdas, execute-api:ManageConnections IAM, DynamoDB TTL, and WebSocketEndpoint output; (5) test/handler.test.ts imports the REAL ws.ts pure helpers and meaningfully tests room-id format/uniqueness, scoreboard sort+ties, the full nextGamePhase lifecycle, scoreSingleAnswer, validateJoinInput normalization/rejection, and the security-critical toParticipantQuestion answerIndex-stripping (hasOwnProperty + JSON scan) — each would fail if the implementation were reverted; (6) frontend deps remain EXACTLY react + react-dom (native WebSocket only, no lockfile), config.ts/amplify.yml/.env.example thread VITE_WS_URL, ws.ts matches the backend contract, and HomePage.tsx reaches BattlePage via an extended View state machine with all single-player flows and the admin page intact. The user MUST run the real build/test/synth and frontend build on a networked host, and set the Amplify env var WS_URL to the WebSocketEndpoint output, per README.
